source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament; complete Acts
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + 4th c.). Codex Bezae (D/05; 5th c.) preserves Western-text Acts with notable expansions in Acts 15 — especially the form of the Apostolic Decree (Western text omits *kai pniktou* 'and what is strangled,' creating a moral-only triad: idolatry + blood [= murder] + porneia, plus adding a Golden-Rule clause). The Western form of the Decree is documented per verse.
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P45 (Chester Beatty I; 3rd c. CE) preserves portions of Acts including Acts 15 (lacunose). P74 (7th c.) preserves Acts 15. P33 (6th c.) preserves portions of Acts 15. The 4th-c. uncials Vaticanus + Sinaiticus remain primary for Acts 15.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017). Boismard-Lamouille for Western readings.
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Bezae (Western) + P45 original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus + Boismard-Lamouille Western edition
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + Metzger UBS Textual Commentary (2nd ed. 1994) ad loc. + the substantial Galatians-2 parallel for the Antioch-Jerusalem dispute.
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Metzger, B. M., *A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament*, 2nd ed. (UBS 1994). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c.). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + (4th c.). Codex Bezae: Cambridge UL Nn.II.41 (5th c.). Barrett ICC 1994-1998 (vol 2); Bock BECNT 2007; Bauckham, R., 'James and the Jerusalem Church' in Bauckham ed. *The Book of Acts in Its Palestinian Setting* (Eerdmans 1995); Bruce NICNT 1988; Conzelmann Hermeneia 1987; Fitzmyer AB 1998; Haenchen 1971; Pervo Hermeneia 2009; Keener 2012-2015 (vol 3 covers Acts 15); Witherington 1998; Wilson *Luke and the Law* (Cambridge 1983); Lieu *Christian Identity in the Jewish and Graeco-Roman World* (Oxford 2004); Bockmuehl, M., 'The Noachide Commandments and New Testament Ethics,' *Revue Biblique* 102 (1995) 72-101.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT (Alexandrian text-type). Western-text variants per Codex Bezae are documented per verse where significant — particularly the well-known divergence in the form of the Apostolic Decree (vv.19-21, 28-29). The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra appear abbreviated in the uncials.

verses.text: Καί τινες κατελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐδίδασκον τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι Ἐὰν μὴ περιτμηθῆτε τῷ ἔθει τῷ Μωϋσέως, οὐ δύνασθε σωθῆναι.
verses.translit: Kai tines katelthontes apo tēs Ioudaias edidaskon tous adelphous hoti Ean mē peritmēthēte tō ethei tō Mōuseōs, ou dynasthe sōthēnai.
verses.notes: **JERUSALEM COUNCIL OPENING — THE CIRCUMCISION CONTROVERSY**. Unnamed Judean teachers arrive in Antioch insisting on circumcision-as-salvific-requirement for Gentile believers. This is the Lukan setup; Galatians 2:11-14 (Paul's own account, partially overlapping) names Cephas/Peter and James-emissaries and presents a more conflictual scene. Bauckham 1995; Pervo Hermeneia 367-371.

verses.text: γενομένης δὲ στάσεως καὶ ζητήσεως οὐκ ὀλίγης τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρναβᾷ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔταξαν ἀναβαίνειν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρναβᾶν καί τινας ἄλλους ἐξ αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ πρεσβυτέρους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ περὶ τοῦ ζητήματος τούτου.
verses.translit: genomenēs de staseōs kai zētēseōs ouk oligēs tō Paulō kai tō Barnaba pros autous etaxan anabainein Paulon kai Barnaban kai tinas allous ex autōn pros tous apostolous kai presbyterous eis Ierousalēm peri tou zētēmatos toutou.
verses.notes: *staseōs kai zētēseōs ouk oligēs* (no small dissension and debate) — Lukan litotes. Antioch sends a delegation to Jerusalem. Parallel Gal 2:1 ("after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus also with me"). The Acts/Galatians relationship is one of the most-debated chronology-questions in NT scholarship (do Gal 2 + Acts 15 narrate the same event?).

verses.text: οἱ μὲν οὖν προπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας διήρχοντο τήν τε Φοινίκην καὶ Σαμάρειαν ἐκδιηγούμενοι τὴν ἐπιστροφὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν, καὶ ἐποίουν χαρὰν μεγάλην πᾶσι τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς.
verses.translit: hoi men oun propemphthentes hypo tēs ekklēsias diērchonto tēn te Phoinikēn kai Samareian ekdiēgoumenoi tēn epistrophēn tōn ethnōn, kai epoioun charan megalēn pasi tois adelphois.
verses.notes: Travel-route Antioch → Phoenicia (Tyre/Sidon) → Samaria → Jerusalem. *tēn epistrophēn tōn ethnōn* (the conversion of the Gentiles) — the rhetorically-loaded news of the report.

verses.text: παραγενόμενοι δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ παρεδέχθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀνήγγειλάν τε ὅσα ὁ θεὸς ἐποίησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: paragenomenoi de eis Ierousalēm paredechthēsan apo tēs ekklēsias kai tōn apostolōn kai tōn presbyterōn, anēngeilan te hosa ho theos epoiēsen met’ autōn.
verses.notes: Tripartite Jerusalem reception: ekklēsia + apostles + elders. Lukan three-tiered church-structure.

verses.text: ἐξανέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς αἱρέσεως τῶν Φαρισαίων πεπιστευκότες, λέγοντες ὅτι δεῖ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς παραγγέλλειν τε τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως.
verses.translit: exanestēsan de tines tōn apo tēs haireseōs tōn Pharisaiōn pepisteukotes, legontes hoti dei peritemnein autous parangellein te tērein ton nomon Mōuseōs.
verses.notes: *tōn ahaireseōs tōn Pharisaiōn pepisteukotes* (those of the sect of the Pharisees who had believed) — a Jewish-Christian Pharisaic-Torah-keeping faction (cross-corpus Paul self-identifies as a Pharisee in 23:6; 26:5; Phil 3:5). Their position: full Torah-observance + circumcision required for Gentile-Christian salvation.

verses.text: Συνήχθησάν τε οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἰδεῖν περὶ τοῦ λόγου τούτου.
verses.translit: Synēchthēsan te hoi apostoloi kai hoi presbyteroi idein peri tou logou toutou.
verses.notes: Formal council convened — apostles + elders. The narrative-shape resembles Jewish-Synagogue / Sanhedrin deliberative procedure.

verses.text: πολλῆς δὲ ζητήσεως γενομένης ἀναστὰς Πέτρος εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἀφ’ ἡμερῶν ἀρχαίων ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξελέξατο ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ στόματός μου ἀκοῦσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὸν λόγον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου καὶ πιστεῦσαι·
verses.translit: pollēs de zētēseōs genomenēs anastas Petros eipen pros autous· Andres adelphoi, hymeis epistasthe hoti aph’ hēmerōn archaiōn en hymin exelexato ho theos dia tou stomatos mou akousai ta ethnē ton logon tou euangeliou kai pisteusai·
verses.notes: **PETER'S SPEECH** — the last appearance of Peter in Acts. *aph’ hēmerōn archaiōn* (from days of old) refers to the Cornelius-event of Acts 10-11. Peter's intervention is the Lukan-Acts pivot: the apostle most associated with Jewish-Christian observance endorses Gentile-inclusion-without-circumcision.

verses.text: καὶ ὁ καρδιογνώστης θεὸς ἐμαρτύρησεν αὐτοῖς δοὺς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καθὼς καὶ ἡμῖν,
verses.translit: kai ho kardiognōstēs theos emartyrēsen autois dous to pneuma to hagion kathōs kai hēmin,
verses.notes: *kardiognōstēs* (knower of hearts) — biblical-Jewish divine-epithet (cf. 1 Kgs 8:39; Ps 7:9; Jer 17:10). Peter's argument: Gentile Pentecost (10:44-46) = same Spirit-gift as the Jewish-disciple Pentecost (ch. 2).

verses.text: καὶ οὐθὲν διέκρινεν μεταξὺ ἡμῶν τε καὶ αὐτῶν, τῇ πίστει καθαρίσας τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: kai outhen diekrinen metaxy hēmōn te kai autōn, tē pistei katharisas tas kardias autōn.
verses.notes: *outhen diekrinen* (made no distinction) — anti-purity-distinction argument. *tē pistei katharisas tas kardias* (cleansing their hearts by faith) — a Pauline-sounding phrase in Peter's mouth (Lukan harmonization of apostolic-theology).

verses.text: νῦν οὖν τί πειράζετε τὸν θεόν, ἐπιθεῖναι ζυγὸν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τῶν μαθητῶν ὃν οὔτε οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν οὔτε ἡμεῖς ἰσχύσαμεν βαστάσαι;
verses.translit: nyn oun ti peirazete ton theon, epitheinai zygon epi ton trachēlon tōn mathētōn hon oute hoi pateres hēmōn oute hēmeis ischysamen bastasai?
verses.notes: *zygon* (yoke) for Torah-observance. Peter's striking concession that 'neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear' the yoke — a notably Pauline-style critique (cf. Gal 3:10; 5:1) again voiced by Peter.

verses.text: ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ πιστεύομεν σωθῆναι καθ’ ὃν τρόπον κἀκεῖνοι.
verses.translit: alla dia tēs charitos tou kyriou Iēsou pisteuomen sōthēnai kath’ hon tropon kakeinoi.
verses.notes: *dia tēs charitos* (through the grace) — soteriology-by-grace. The Lukan-Acts Peter speaks Pauline soteriology — this is the harmonizing-tendency in Acts that scholarship debates (Pervo, Conzelmann).

verses.text: Ἐσίγησεν δὲ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος, καὶ ἤκουον Βαρναβᾶ καὶ Παύλου ἐξηγουμένων ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν δι’ αὐτῶν.
verses.translit: Esigēsen de pan to plēthos, kai ēkouon Barnaba kai Paulou exēgoumenōn hosa epoiēsen ho theos sēmeia kai terata en tois ethnesin di’ autōn.
verses.notes: Lukan order: Barnabas BEFORE Paul (reverting to the pre-elevation order; cf. 14:14 vs. 13:13). Suggests Barnabas's continued seniority in the Jerusalem context. *sēmeia kai terata* — signs-and-wonders argument as evidentiary.

verses.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ σιγῆσαι αὐτοὺς ἀπεκρίθη Ἰάκωβος λέγων· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἀκούσατέ μου.
verses.translit: Meta de to sigēsai autous apekrithē Iakōbos legōn· Andres adelphoi, akousate mou.
verses.notes: **JAMES'S SPEECH BEGINS**. *Iakōbos* = James the brother of Jesus, Jerusalem-church leader. His final-word position signals his decisive authority. Cross-corpus Gal 2:9 'James and Cephas and John, those reputed to be pillars.'

verses.text: Συμεὼν ἐξηγήσατο καθὼς πρῶτον ὁ θεὸς ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν λαὸν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Symeōn exēgēsato kathōs prōton ho theos epeskepsato labein ex ethnōn laon tō onomati autou.
verses.notes: *Symeōn* = Semitic form of Simon/Peter — the only place James uses this archaizing-form (the Hebrew/Aramaic Šim‘ōn). *laon tō onomati autou* (a people for his name) — striking phrase, applies the *laos* term traditionally reserved for Israel to the Gentiles.

verses.text: καὶ τούτῳ συμφωνοῦσιν οἱ λόγοι τῶν προφητῶν, καθὼς γέγραπται·
verses.translit: kai toutō symphōnousin hoi logoi tōn prophētōn, kathōs gegraptai·
verses.notes: James introduces an Amos 9 LXX citation. The use of LXX (not MT) here is striking for a Jerusalem speech — possibly a Lukan literary choice, or possibly reflects diaspora-Greek scripture-use even in Jerusalem.

verses.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναστρέψω καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσω τὴν σκηνὴν Δαυὶδ τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν, καὶ τὰ κατεσκαμμένα αὐτῆς ἀνοικοδομήσω καὶ ἀνορθώσω αὐτήν,
verses.translit: Meta tauta anastrepsō kai anoikodomēsō tēn skēnēn Dauid tēn peptōkuian, kai ta kateskammena autēs anoikodomēsō kai anorthōsō autēn,
verses.notes: **AMOS 9:11-12 LXX CITATION** begins. *tēn skēnēn Dauid tēn peptōkuian* (the fallen tent of David) — Davidic-restoration. The LXX rendering crucially differs from the MT (which reads about Israel possessing the remnant of Edom); the LXX has 'the remnant of humans' (*hoi kataloipoi tōn anthrōpōn*) — apparently reading Hebrew *adam* (humans) for MT *edom*. This LXX-variant is load-bearing for James's argument: only the LXX-text supports Gentile-inclusion via Davidic-restoration.

verses.text: ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν κύριον, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐφ’ οὓς ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπ’ αὐτούς, λέγει κύριος ποιῶν ταῦτα
verses.translit: hopōs an ekzētēsōsin hoi kataloipoi tōn anthrōpōn ton kyrion, kai panta ta ethnē eph’ hous epikeklētai to onoma mou ep’ autous, legei kyrios poiōn tauta
verses.notes: *panta ta ethnē* (all the nations / Gentiles) — the load-bearing phrase. *eph’ hous epikeklētai to onoma mou* (upon whom my name has been called) — biblical formula for divine ownership (cross-corpus 2 Sam 7:23; Isa 63:19).

verses.text: γνωστὰ ἀπ’ αἰῶνος.
verses.translit: gnōsta ap’ aiōnos.
verses.notes: *gnōsta ap’ aiōnos* (known from of old). Variant: Western text + later Byzantine MSS expand to *gnōston ap’ aiōnos estin tō theō panta ta erga autou* ("known to God from of old are all his works"). The shorter NA28/SBLGNT reading is preferred (lectio brevior + Vaticanus + Sinaiticus support).

verses.text: διὸ ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν,
verses.translit: dio egō krinō mē parenochlein tois apo tōn ethnōn epistrephousin epi ton theon,
verses.notes: **JAMES'S RULING**. *egō krinō* (I judge / decide) — singular first-person decisive authority. *parenochlein* (trouble / harass) — keep the burden light. This is the load-bearing JerusalemCouncil-decision verb.

verses.text: ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι αὐτοῖς τοῦ ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων καὶ τῆς πορνείας καὶ τοῦ πνικτοῦ καὶ τοῦ αἵματος·
verses.translit: alla episteilai autois tou apechesthai tōn alisgēmatōn tōn eidōlōn kai tēs porneias kai tou pniktou kai tou haimatos·
verses.notes: **THE APOSTOLIC DECREE — FIRST FORMULATION**. Four-fold abstention: (1) *alisgēmatōn tōn eidōlōn* (pollutions of idols / idol-sacrifices); (2) *porneia* (sexual immorality); (3) *pniktou* (strangled meat — animal not properly bled); (4) *haimatos* (blood — eating blood). Cross-corpus **Lev 17-18** (the resident-alien laws — idol-sacrifice [Lev 17:7-9], blood-eating [Lev 17:10-14], strangled/non-drained meat [Lev 17:15-16], forbidden sexual unions [Lev 18:6-23]). The Lev 17-18 background is decisive in modern scholarship (Bauckham 1995; Bockmuehl 1995) — the Decree is the Gentile equivalent of the Torah's *ger toshav* (resident alien) requirements. Cross-corpus also to the seven **Noahide commandments** in rabbinic tradition (t. Avodah Zarah 8:4) — though the Noahide list is later codified. **MAJOR TEXTUAL VARIANT**: Codex Bezae + Western text OMITS *kai tou pniktou* and ADDS a Golden-Rule clause (*kai hosa mē thelousin heautois ginesthai, heterois mē poiein*), producing a moral-only triad: idolatry + porneia + blood [= bloodshed/murder]. This Western reading is preferred by some scholars (e.g., older Catholic exegesis) but the four-fold Alexandrian reading is preferred by NA28/SBLGNT and modern critical consensus.

verses.text: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ ἐκ γενεῶν ἀρχαίων κατὰ πόλιν τοὺς κηρύσσοντας αὐτὸν ἔχει ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκόμενος.
verses.translit: Mōusēs gar ek geneōn archaiōn kata polin tous kēryssontas auton echei en tais synagōgais kata pan sabbaton anaginōskomenos.
verses.notes: **JAMES'S RATIONALE** for the four-fold restriction: Moses is read every Sabbath in every-city synagogue, so the basic ethical-purity requirements are already universally known. The clause has been variously read as: (a) preserving Jewish-Christian fellowship (the Decree makes table-fellowship possible); (b) accommodating diaspora-synagogue ethics; (c) re-codifying the Lev 17-18 *ger toshav* framework universally.

verses.text: Τότε ἔδοξε τοῖς ἀποστόλοις καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις σὺν ὅλῃ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐκλεξαμένους ἄνδρας ἐξ αὐτῶν πέμψαι εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν σὺν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ Βαρναβᾷ, Ἰούδαν τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν καὶ Σιλᾶν, ἄνδρας ἡγουμένους ἐν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς,
verses.translit: Tote edoxe tois apostolois kai tois presbyterois syn holē tē ekklēsia eklexamenous andras ex autōn pempsai eis Antiocheian syn tō Paulō kai Barnaba, Ioudan ton kaloumenon Barsabban kai Silan, andras hēgoumenous en tois adelphois,
verses.notes: *edoxe tois apostolois kai tois presbyterois syn holē tē ekklēsia* — the consensus-decision formula (cf. v.25 *edoxen hēmin*). Judas-Barsabbas + Silas as bearers (Silas later becomes Paul's partner from 15:40). Decision-making process: apostles + elders deliberate, whole church consents.

verses.text: γράψαντες διὰ χειρὸς αὐτῶν· Οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἀδελφοὶ τοῖς κατὰ τὴν Ἀντιόχειαν καὶ Συρίαν καὶ Κιλικίαν ἀδελφοῖς τοῖς ἐξ ἐθνῶν χαίρειν.
verses.translit: grapsantes dia cheiros autōn· Hoi apostoloi kai hoi presbyteroi adelphoi tois kata tēn Antiocheian kai Syrian kai Kilikian adelphois tois ex ethnōn chairein.
verses.notes: **OFFICIAL DECREE-LETTER OPENING**. Standard Hellenistic letter-prescript: senders + addressees + *chairein* (greetings). Region: Antioch + Syria + Cilicia (Paul's homeland-region, the area of his Tarsus-base and early Antiochene mission).

verses.text: Ἐπειδὴ ἠκούσαμεν ὅτι τινὲς ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐτάραξαν ὑμᾶς λόγοις ἀνασκευάζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν, οἷς οὐ διεστειλάμεθα,
verses.translit: Epeidē ēkousamen hoti tines ex hēmōn etaraxan hymas logois anaskeuazontes tas psychas hymōn, hois ou diesteilametha,
verses.notes: *tines ex hēmōn etaraxan hymas* (some from us troubled you) — Jerusalem disavows the v.1 unnamed teachers. *hois ou diesteilametha* (whom we did not authorize).

verses.text: ἔδοξεν ἡμῖν γενομένοις ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐκλεξαμένοις ἄνδρας πέμψαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς σὺν τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς ἡμῶν Βαρναβᾷ καὶ Παύλῳ,
verses.translit: edoxen hēmin genomenois homothymadon eklexamenois andras pempsai pros hymas syn tois agapētois hēmōn Barnaba kai Paulō,
verses.notes: *edoxen hēmin* (it seemed [good] to us) — formal Hellenistic decree-language (cf. Athenian assembly-decrees *edoxe tē boulē kai tō dēmō*). *homothymadon* (with one accord) — Lukan-Acts consensus keyword.

verses.text: ἀνθρώποις παραδεδωκόσι τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
verses.translit: anthrōpois paradedōkosi tas psychas autōn hyper tou onomatos tou kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou.
verses.notes: Endorsement of Barnabas + Paul as those who have risked their lives — references the persecutions of 13:50-14:20.

verses.text: ἀπεστάλκαμεν οὖν Ἰούδαν καὶ Σιλᾶν, καὶ αὐτοὺς διὰ λόγου ἀπαγγέλλοντας τὰ αὐτά.
verses.translit: apestalkamen oun Ioudan kai Silan, kai autous dia logou apangellontas ta auta.
verses.notes: Oral-confirmation alongside the written letter — standard ancient diplomatic practice.

verses.text: ἔδοξεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ ἡμῖν μηδὲν πλέον ἐπιτίθεσθαι ὑμῖν βάρος πλὴν τούτων τῶν ἐπάναγκες,
verses.translit: edoxen gar tō pneumati tō hagiō kai hēmin mēden pleon epitithesthai hymin baros plēn toutōn tōn epanankes,
verses.notes: **FAMOUS DECREE-FORMULA**. *edoxen tō pneumati tō hagiō kai hēmin* (it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us) — joint Spirit-and-council authorship. *tōn epanankes* (these necessary things) — fixed list to follow.

verses.text: ἀπέχεσθαι εἰδωλοθύτων καὶ αἵματος καὶ πνικτῶν καὶ πορνείας· ἐξ ὧν διατηροῦντες ἑαυτοὺς εὖ πράξετε. ἔρρωσθε.
verses.translit: apechesthai eidōlothytōn kai haimatos kai pniktōn kai porneias· ex hōn diatērountes heautous eu praxete. Errōsthe.
verses.notes: **THE APOSTOLIC DECREE — FORMAL FORMULATION**. Four-fold abstention list (slightly different order from v.20): (1) *eidōlothytōn* (idol-sacrifices); (2) *haimatos* (blood); (3) *pniktōn* (strangled meat); (4) *porneia* (sexual immorality). Order swap: vv.20 lists pollutions+porneia+pniktou+haimatos; v.29 lists eidōlothytōn+haimatos+pniktōn+porneia. **MAJOR TEXTUAL VARIANT**: Codex Bezae + Western text again OMITS *pniktōn* and ADDS the negative Golden Rule (*kai hosa mē thelete heautois ginesthai, heterō mē poiein*) — yielding the moral-only triad. Some patristic citations support the Western form (Cyprian, Tertullian). NA28/SBLGNT/modern critical consensus retains the four-fold Alexandrian reading. The form of the Decree continues to be debated (Bockmuehl 1995; Bauckham 1995). *errōsthe* (farewell) — standard Hellenistic letter-closing. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do not pre-resolve toward Raëlian readings of dietary-prohibitions or sexual-ethics; preserve.

verses.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀπολυθέντες κατῆλθον εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, καὶ συναγαγόντες τὸ πλῆθος ἐπέδωκαν τὴν ἐπιστολήν·
verses.translit: Hoi men oun apolythentes katēlthon eis Antiocheian, kai synagagontes to plēthos epedōkan tēn epistolēn·
verses.notes: Delegation returns to Antioch; assembles the congregation; delivers the letter.

verses.text: ἀναγνόντες δὲ ἐχάρησαν ἐπὶ τῇ παρακλήσει.
verses.translit: anagnontes de echarēsan epi tē paraklēsei.
verses.notes: *paraklēsis* (encouragement). Antiochene reception is positive — Lukan idealization of consensus.

verses.text: Ἰούδας τε καὶ Σιλᾶς, καὶ αὐτοὶ προφῆται ὄντες, διὰ λόγου πολλοῦ παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἐπεστήριξαν·
verses.translit: Ioudas te kai Silas, kai autoi prophētai ontes, dia logou pollou parekalesan tous adelphous kai epestērixan·
verses.notes: Judas + Silas identified as prophets — the Lukan-Acts prophetic-ministry charism in the early church (cf. 11:27; 13:1; 21:9-10).

verses.text: ποιήσαντες δὲ χρόνον ἀπελύθησαν μετ’ εἰρήνης ἀπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστείλαντας αὐτούς.
verses.translit: poiēsantes de chronon apelythēsan met’ eirēnēs apo tōn adelphōn pros tous aposteilantas autous.
verses.notes: After some time, return to Jerusalem. *met’ eirēnēs* — peaceful dismissal.

**MISSING / SPURIOUS VERSE**. NA28/SBLGNT/UBS5/THGNT OMIT v.34 entirely — it is ABSENT in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + most Alexandrian witnesses. Codex Bezae + Western text + the Textus Receptus preserve an interpolation: *edoxe de tō Sila epimeinai autou* ("but it seemed good to Silas to remain there") — a scribal harmonization to explain Silas's continued presence at v.40. The longer Western form expands further: *kai monos Ioudas eporeuthē* ("and Judas alone went"). The variant is documented per critical apparatus but not reproduced in the Alexandrian text. Verse-number preserved as a hole per critical convention.

verses.text: Παῦλος δὲ καὶ Βαρναβᾶς διέτριβον ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι μετὰ καὶ ἑτέρων πολλῶν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου.
verses.translit: Paulos de kai Barnabas dietribon en Antiocheia didaskontes kai euangelizomenoi meta kai heterōn pollōn ton logon tou kyriou.
verses.notes: Continued Antioch-base ministry. *meta kai heterōn pollōn* (with many others also) — hints at the broader Antiochene teaching-team.

verses.text: Μετὰ δέ τινας ἡμέρας εἶπεν πρὸς Βαρναβᾶν Παῦλος· Ἐπιστρέψαντες δὴ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς κατὰ πᾶσαν πόλιν ἐν αἷς κατηγγείλαμεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου, πῶς ἔχουσιν.
verses.translit: Meta de tinas hēmeras eipen pros Barnaban Paulos· Epistrepsantes dē episkepsōmetha tous adelphous kata pasan polin en hais katēngeilamen ton logon tou kyriou, pōs echousin.
verses.notes: Paul proposes the second-missionary-journey return-tour. Note Lukan order has shifted back: *Paulos* first, *Barnaban* second (Paul is now leading).

verses.text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐβούλετο συμπαραλαβεῖν καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην τὸν καλούμενον Μᾶρκον·
verses.translit: Barnabas de ebouleto symparalabein kai ton Iōannēn ton kaloumenon Markon·
verses.notes: Barnabas wants John Mark (his cousin — Col 4:10). Sets up the famous disagreement.

verses.text: Παῦλος δὲ ἠξίου, τὸν ἀποστάντα ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Παμφυλίας καὶ μὴ συνελθόντα αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἔργον, μὴ συμπαραλαμβάνειν τοῦτον.
verses.translit: Paulos de ēxiou, ton apostanta ap’ autōn apo Pamphylias kai mē synelthonta autois eis to ergon, mē symparalambanein touton.
verses.notes: Paul refuses — citing Mark's earlier defection at Perga (13:13). *apostanta* (deserted) — harsh vocabulary.

verses.text: ἐγένετο δὲ παροξυσμὸς ὥστε ἀποχωρισθῆναι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων, τόν τε Βαρναβᾶν παραλαβόντα τὸν Μᾶρκον ἐκπλεῦσαι εἰς Κύπρον.
verses.translit: egeneto de paroxysmos hōste apochōristhēnai autous ap’ allēlōn, ton te Barnaban paralabonta ton Markon ekpleusai eis Kypron.
verses.notes: **FAMOUS PAUL/BARNABAS SPLIT**. *paroxysmos* (sharp disagreement) — vivid vocabulary (LXX Deut 29:28; medical: paroxysm of fever). Barnabas + Mark go to Cyprus (Barnabas's native island, 4:36). The split is one of the rare narrative-disharmonies in Lukan-Acts.

verses.text: Παῦλος δὲ ἐπιλεξάμενος Σιλᾶν ἐξῆλθεν παραδοθεὶς τῇ χάριτι τοῦ κυρίου ὑπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν,
verses.translit: Paulos de epilexamenos Silan exēlthen paradotheis tē chariti tou kyriou hypo tōn adelphōn,
verses.notes: Paul takes Silas. Sets up the second-missionary-journey through 18:22.

verses.text: διήρχετο δὲ τὴν Συρίαν καὶ Κιλικίαν ἐπιστηρίζων τὰς ἐκκλησίας.
verses.translit: diērcheto de tēn Syrian kai Kilikian epistērizōn tas ekklēsias.
verses.notes: Syria + Cilicia overland — Paul's homeland-route. *epistērizōn* (strengthening) — Lukan-Acts pastoral-vocabulary. Chapter ends with mission-renewal.
